speaker: Ms Janet Ang
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry in light of Singapore's ambition to become a global trading hub for climate-related services, what is being done to ensure the credibility of carbon products to be traded through Singapore and to reduce Singapore's exposure to the risks of carbon trading.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry in view of Singapore’s import of the first carbon-neutral liquified natural gas cargo (a) what agreement is in place to require the cargo suppliers to provide a statement of the greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions of each cargo; and (b) what mechanisms will be applied to monitor the carbon credits used to offset the GHG emissions of each cargo.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Our country, Singapore's robust legislative, commodities trading and financial services foundation has put us in a good position to grow an internationally-trusted carbon services and trading eco-system in Asia.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Today, the carbon trading eco-system in this region comprises primarily of the trading of voluntary carbon credits.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: These credits are used by companies to meet their voluntary corporate climate targets, alongside other decarbonisation strategies.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The main risk for buyers in voluntary carbon credits markets has been on the integrity and the quality of such carbon credits.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The Government is working with industry, with international and local experts, as well as environmental groups to address this risk.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Second, we are exploring the use of technology to improve the verification of these credits.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In December 2020, DBS and Temasek, with Google Cloud, NUS, Verra and the World Bank as partners, launched the Sustainable Xcelerator to improve the efficiency of verifying emissions reductions and sequestration.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Third, the Emerging Stronger Taskforce Alliance for Action on Sustainability is also looking at establishing a marketplace and exchange to improve transparency in carbon credit transactions.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Alongside carbon trading, there are opportunities in the carbon services market.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For example, we aim to anchor key activities in Singapore, such as in project development, carbon credits trading, financing and measurement, reporting and verification services.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We will continue to work with like-minded partners to support the development of an overall well-functioning global carbon market, and build capabilities and capacities to grow our local eco-system.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To answer Miss Cheryl Chan's question, organisations can use carbon credits, alongside other decarbonisation strategies, to mitigate the greenhouse emissions resulting from their operating units or businesses.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Today, this is done on a voluntary basis to meet companies' climate targets.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Pavilion Energy then offsets these greenhouse gas emissions by retiring a corresponding amount of carbon credits sourced from its portfolio of carbon offset projects in Peru and China.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Pavilion Energy has published the amount of emissions it has offset from the two projects, which are certified under the Verified Carbon Standard and the Climate, Community and Biodiversity Standard.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: While the Government today does not regulate voluntary offsetting activities, we are working with the industry, international and local experts, as well as many environmental groups to develop – as I have alluded to earlier on – a taxonomy and guidelines on the quality of these carbon credits.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The guidelines can then be adopted by companies undertaking commercial agreements in carbon offset activities.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: I am heartened that we are taking a lot of active actions in terms of what we are doing around carbon credits and how we are going to measure that on an international basis.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: I have one supplementary question for the Minister.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Given the fact that we are now trying to do all these carbon sequestration with other countries overseas, over time, there will come a challenge between countries putting up their carbon taxes as well as how we are going to exchange this in terms of carbon credits.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Is the Minister able to give us an insight on what are Singapore's plans if the carbon taxes do rise to a certain significant sum in other countries, because it does not make economic sense in terms of carbon credit offsets between countries?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Indeed, I think this is a point of concern alongside many, many other competing concerns that we have.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We have also got an AfA that we have set up to look at sustainability in terms of a broader overall picture not just from the carbon credit, carbon trading and carbon tax's point of view but to see how sustainable they would be on top of our overall energy story in our own country's energy roadmap moving forward for the next foreseeable 10, 20 to 30 years.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We are happy to take feedback and suggestions and, as I have alluded to earlier in my answer, we are actively sourcing and working with partners not just locally, internationally, but as well as with many of the environmental partners to see how we can nuance this in a very, very good and strategic path to ensure not just our own sustainability but, more importantly, our own resilience, moving forward.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: There were recent media reports on the sale of meaningless carbon credits by a top US supplier.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: I originally had two supplementary questions, but the Minister has answered my second one.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: So, I will just tackle the first one.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: How does the Government plan to increase the awareness amongst Singapore companies with this relatively new product?

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: We know Singapore has worked so hard to attain a stellar reputation as a credible and trusted hub and partner.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: As the Minister has shared just now, I am very excited to hear about all the opportunities as well as the work that we are doing to develop a taxonomy and guidelines and so on.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: How are we going to engage the companies in Singapore so that they will not be scammed or they can be better prepared as they prepare for their alignment to the Singapore Green Plan 2030?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think there are different types of carbon markets today.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: One of the examples is the European Union ETS, which is the world's first carbon market.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Of course, at the international level, discussions are also underway at the UN Conference for Climate Change.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Again, this kind of meetings seeks to recognise the use of carbon credits to offset national emissions.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: They enable companies, individuals to purchase carbon offsets on a voluntary basis to manage their carbon emissions.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This is in addition to other decarbonisation strategies.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: They do not have an intended use for compliance purposes.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, these compliance credits may, in some instances, be purchased by voluntary non-regulated entities.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: They are not broadly accepted into a compliance regime unless they fulfil a broader perspective.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And therein lies the challenge which the hon Member has alluded to.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Many of the companies looking to invest in Singapore, particularly from the semi-conductors to even data centres and so on, they have also moved on to source for many of these carbon credits.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think it is now an opportune moment for us to work collectively together to nuance this approach and, at the same time, bring many of our own enterprises locally, as well as regional SMEs that have decided to sink roots here in Singapore, along with us.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, I thank the Member for highlighting this.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: It is certainly one of those targets that we not just aspire to do, but we have every intention to fulfil.
